observations: Seller confirms verbally that they tested it and that their claims are true, but provides no new photos/videos.
Photos previously provided still do not show readable engine code/part numbers, compressor identification, mileage, or any test evidence (no running video, no scan/compression results).

identity.kind: complete Toyota engine assembly with attached intake/air components and related parts (seller says includes compressor and operators)

claims.claim: Complete engine with compressor and all the operators for Toyota Venza, Camry, Sienna, Highlander,...
claims.evidence: No new photo showing compressor part number/label or a full included-parts inventory; prior photos do not clearly confirm completeness for those specific models.
No shipping/import documents or identifiable Belgium sourcing evidence is visible in the photos.

claims.claim: Tested and working, no knock, low mileage, never opened.
claims.evidence: Seller’s statement only; no new running video, sound recording, scan report, compression/leak-down results, or mileage proof was provided.

risks.risk: Exact engine variant/engine code is not readable; wrong engine can cause fitment/ECU/compatibility issues.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the engine code/label (stamping/plate) and transmission/ECU part numbers, plus a photo showing the compressor part number if included.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a generic used Toyota engine assembly with unknown compatibility (worst-case: may not fit or may require additional parts).

risks.risk: Compressor inclusion/type may be wrong or incomplete.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the A/C compressor with its label/part number and visible connection ports.
risks.if_unproven: Price as engine assembly only (worst-case: compressor not included or not usable).

risks.risk: “No knock / working” not proven remotely without a test recording.
risks.proof: Short start-up video (ideally cold start) showing stable idle and no knocking, plus a mechanic’s sound check note.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not proven working (worst-case: treat as needing inspection/possible repair).

risks.risk: “Never opened / low mileage” cannot be confirmed; leaks or prior repairs may exist.
risks.proof: Photos of gasket surfaces/repair marks and any compression test/leak-down results.
risks.if_unproven: Price as unknown history (worst-case: assume wear and potential leaks).

risks.risk: Completeness of “all the operators” is vague; missing sensors/brackets/mounts/wiring can add cost.
risks.proof: A full inventory/checklist photo showing every included component and connectors.
risks.if_unproven: Price as incomplete/unknown completeness (worst-case: buyer must source missing parts).

proof_requests: Send a short start-up video (cold start if possible) showing the engine running smoothly with no knocking.
Send clear close-up photos of the engine code/label/stamping and the transmission/ECU part numbers.
Send close-up photos of the A/C compressor label/part number (and confirm it is included).
Send compression test or leak-down test results (or a mechanic’s report) and any scan/diagnostic report.
Send an inventory photo/checklist of everything included (sensors, brackets, mounts, hoses, wiring connectors, ECU/TCU if applicable).
response.reason: The seller’s verbal confirmation doesn’t replace missing visual/test evidence. Without new photos/videos showing engine identification and proof of working condition/completeness, the item can’t be priced confidently beyond worst-case assumptions.
